content.text: About the Los Angeles DodgersThe Los Angeles Dodgers enter 2026 chasing something no National League team has ever accomplished: a three-peat. Fresh off back-to-back World Series titles in 2024 and 2025 — the latter a seven-game thriller against the Blue Jays capped by Will Smith's historic extra-inning home run and Yoshinobu Yamamoto's legendary bullpen appearance on zero rest — this franchise has earned the dynasty label from every corner of the baseball world. The roster is arguably the most stacked in modern history, with eight players on nine-figure contracts. Shohei Ohtani enters 2026 as a full-time two-way player from Opening Day for the first time as a Dodger, four-time All-Star Kyle Tucker arrives via a $240 million deal to fortify the lineup, and closer Edwin Díaz shores up the bullpen. Add in Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Tyler Glasnow and Roki Sasaki, and you're looking at a team built to make history all over again.Dodger Stadium holds the highest cumulative fan attendance in Major League Baseball history, and there's a reason four million fans packed the Ravine last year. The energy on a summer night in Chavez Ravine — sunset bleeding over the San Gabriel Mountains, the crack of Ohtani's bat echoing through the stands — is something you feel in your chest. With a $100 million renovation completed ahead of 2025 and additional upgrades rolling out for 2026, the ballpark blends its iconic mid-century charm with a modern gameday experience that few venues in any sport can match. Early-season games carry extra weight this year, too: the championship ring ceremony is set for March 27, and the Dodgers host the Diamondbacks on Opening Day the night before.This is a franchise with nine World Series championships, 26 National League pennants, and 12 NL West titles in the last 13 seasons — sustained excellence that's almost hard to believe. The 2026 season also marks the beginning of the post-Kershaw era, as the beloved lefty retired after 18 seasons in Dodger blue, closing one of the most iconic chapters in franchise history. Manager Dave Roberts, locked in through 2029, leads a club that ESPN described as "an MLB behemoth that isn't going away anytime soon." Yamamoto, the reigning World Series MVP, anchors a six-man rotation alongside Ohtani and Sasaki, giving you a reason to circle just about every home date on the calendar. Whether you've been a Dodgers fan your whole life or you're drawn to the gravity of a team making a legitimate run at baseball immortality, this is the season to be watching.When is the Los Angeles Dodgers Opening Day? Dodgers Opening Day is March 26, 2026.Where do the Los Angeles Dodgers play? The Los Angeles Dodgers play their home games at Dodger Stadium.Dodger Stadium, opened in 1962, is the third-oldest stadium in Major League Baseball and the largest by capacity, seating 56,000 fans. Located in Chavez Ravine, it offers panoramic views of the San Gabriel Mountains, downtown Los Angeles, and the Pacific Ocean on clear days. Known for its clean mid-century design, Dodger Stadium remains one of the most iconic venues in sports.The stadium has hosted numerous historic moments, including Sandy Koufax’s perfect game and Kirk Gibson’s walk-off home run in the 1988 World Series. Recent renovations have added modern amenities, including upgraded concourses and a new center-field plaza. With its rich history and passionate fan base, Dodger Stadium is a cornerstone of baseball tradition.How many World Series have the Los Angeles Dodgers won? The Dodgers have won nine World Series, including going back-to-back in 2024 and 2025. What division do the Los Angeles Dodgers play in? The Dodgers are in the National League West, along with the San Francisco Giants, San Diego Padres, Arizona Diamondbacks and Colorado Rockies.
